Green spaces
Highgate Wood
Visit Highgate Wood
Go to Facebook Go to Twitter Go to LinkedIn Go to Mail
Highgate Wood is a beautiful 70-acre ancient woodland in North London offering a rich mix of wildlife, heritage and community spaces. With its diverse woodland habitat, popular café with terrace, large playground, and well‑used sports field, it provides a peaceful escape for families, walkers and nature lovers alike.
As a designated Green Flag and Green Heritage Site, Highgate Wood is home to a wide variety of birds, bats, moths, fungi and historic features, making it a destination for those seeking nature, biodiversity and outdoor recreation in London.
The Wood is operated as a charity (Charity No. 232986).
Closure due to high winds
Highgate Wood contains ancient woodland and lots of old trees. If wind speeds are forecast to be 37mph or above, the Wood may need to be closed for safety reasons and at short notice. We will update social media with any planned closures wherever possible.
Events in Highgate Wood
Events in Highgate Wood are carefully managed to balance community use with the protection of its ancient woodland environment, ensuring activities do not adversely impact habitats or visitor experience. Find out more about Event Applications .
We are not taking any more applications for new events in 2026. If you would like to apply to hold a public or community event in 2027, please fill in the Event Application Form .
Exploring Highgate Wood
Their are waymarking signposts in the Wood but you can also find your way around with our map or by using what3words (see links below).
Follow our self guided historic trail to learn more about the history of the Wood.
Find out more about the Roman history of Highgate Wood
Visit ‘Highgate’s Roman Story’ exhibition in the refurbished Information Hut to uncover the story of the Roman potters from nearly 2,000 years ago. See one of their pottery kilns fully on display for the first time, and learn about the archaeological excavations that brought this story to life.
The new displays opened in October 2026, following the completion of Friends of Highgate Roman Kiln’s ‘Firing London’s Imagination’ project, 2023 – 26, supported by The National Lottery Heritage Fund. Further information can be found on the Roman Kiln webpage.

Getting here
Public transport
Highgate Wood is connected to public transport by Highgate Station (5 minute walk away) on the Northern Line, as well as by several bus routes including the 43, 134 and the 234.
Visit TfL's Journey Planner to plan your trip.
Parking
Highgate Wood doesn't have a car park. There are two bays for blue badge holders within the Wood, near the café. ///novel.successes.wings
Entrance for cars with blue badges, is the Onslow Gate. ///strike.closer.finely
Limited street parking is available in the surrounding area with restrictions.
Accessibility
Highgate Wood is an ancient woodland and while some of the paths are tarmacked, others are rough unmade paths which can be muddy in wet weather.
There are two wheelchair accessible toilets in the Wood. One is by the playground and is 1.9 by 1.65m in dimension (what3words location: ///song.towns.wiser )and one is by the café and is 2.5m by 2.5m in dimension (what3words location: ///award.sheep.accent ). Both are accessible with a Radar key.

Cycling
As stated in our byelaws , and in order to protect the ancient woodland, cycling is not permitted anywhere in Highgate Wood.
